task_name: Voltcast - Podcast short and audio treatment
client_brief:
Episode 42 is the three power station test, and what I need from you is the short form pack that goes out with it, not the long episode.

Everything I am sending is silent picture. There is no usable production audio on any of it, so build these the way our shorts already play in the feed with the sound off: the verdict lives in the on screen text you set. Nothing on screen may claim I said something, and do not write captions for speech that is not on the file. A cleared instrumental bed is in the pack as voltcast_bed.wav. Use that and nothing else.

Final handoff

Episode 42 verdict short: one named export, square, twelve to fifteen seconds, music bed only. It carries my verdict order for the three units and the episode number. Build it from at least three different shots. Do not loop one clip to fill the length.

Verdict short vertical cutdown: one named export, upright, eight to ten seconds, music bed only. Same story told tighter, cut from the same shots.

Podcast episode cover: one named export, square still, as before.

House rules. The bug goes bottom right on everything and it stays small. Volt Orange is the only accent. The Meridian logo lives on the sponsor card and nowhere else, so keep it off the cover. Unit names are spelled the way my notes spell them.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film, and no film in this pack carries speech.

Live action edits require adequate distinct footage. Looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2020 in Portland, Oregon. A two-person operation with a mid six-figure subscriber base, publishing several times a week.
brand_identity.about: Voltcast is an independent consumer-tech review channel run by two people out of Portland. We buy or borrow the gear, run it hard, and say what we actually think. Episodes go out long-form to the main feed plus vertical and square shorts. About a third of the revenue is sponsor money, so the grid has to look like one channel and the sponsor read has to be exactly right.
brand_identity.audience: Enthusiast buyers and everyday shoppers who want an honest verdict before they spend. They follow us because we are not the manufacturer, and they can tell the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-tier creator economy. A sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The channel has to read as a credible independent reviewer, never as broadcast gloss and never as raw phone-shot filler.
brand_identity.typography: PP Radio Grotesk Bold carries the verdict, one word only, all caps, tracked minus 15 units and optically scaled until it touches both card margins, Volt Orange on Card Charcoal: 96 px on the 1080 square, 120 px on the vertical, four times the body size, so the word lands before anything else is read. PP Radio Grotesk Medium sets the episode label at 40 px tracked 80. Inter Regular sets body and sponsor copy at 30 px on 42 px leading, Inter Medium tabular figures for specs at 34 px, disclosure never below 24 px, print sheet 9 pt. Never let the verdict run to two words.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, dry, and unhyped. We talk like a person who has actually used the thing. Sponsor copy runs as written and the disclosure line is exact. We never oversell.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The channel bug exists only as a flat export on white and we have no editable brand kit. On-screen cards get rebuilt from scratch every episode, which is the problem we want solved. We need the bug prepared as reusable artwork and the card set delivered as a file we can reopen and change each week.
brand_identity.values: Independence from the manufacturers we cover, honesty about what we tested, consistency across the grid, and respect for the audience that trusts the verdict.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The verdict is one word only, all caps in PP Radio Grotesk Bold, tracked minus 15 units and optically scaled until it touches both card margins, Volt Orange on Card Charcoal.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
